title: Ariyil Shukoor murder case verdict: Milestone in legal battle that stretched for a 'life term', and is far from over
content: Kochi: Fourteen years and seven months is what it took for the first major legal verdict on the 2012 murder of Muslim Students Federation (MSF) leader Ariyil Abdul Shukoor. And though 13 of the accused have been convicted, Shukoor's family is yet to give up. His mother, P C Aathikka, who had gone up to the Supreme Court to get the CBI to probe the case, and other relatives have indicated that they might appeal against the acquittal of 18 of the accused, including CPM State Committee member and the then district secretary P Jayarajan and the then Kalliasseri MLA T V Rajesh, who were accused of the conspiracy to kill Shukoor. The court on Thursday found seven of the 15 accused guilty under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code for directly participating in the murder. They were K V Sumesh (A1), a driver with the Kasargod unit of the Kerala Fire Force Department; Anoop P (A3), Pavithran (A7), P V Manoharan (A9), N P Dineshan alias Myna Dineshan (A10), Bijumon (A12) and Shijin Mohan (A15). Six others, E P Radhakrishnan (A14), K V Sajith (A16), V V Mohanan (A25), M V Purushothaman (A26), P K Ajithkumar (A27) and P P Sureshan (A28), were also found guilty of murder and attempt to murder of Shukoor's friend Zakaria, who was the main eyewitness in the case. They were accused of illegally detaining and threatening Shukoor, Zakaria, Harris and Salam, who had taken refuge in a house during the attack. Of the six others accused of being part of the group that attacked Shukoor, Ganesh (A2), Vijesh (A4), K Prakashan (A5), Latheesh (A8), C N Mohanan (A11) and Nithin (A13) were acquitted. The 18 acquitted also included P Jayarajan, T V Rajesh and Shyamjith (A19), son of CPM state secretary M V Govindan. The prosecution had accused Jayarajan and Rajesh of conspiring to eliminate Shukoor. The court held that the prosecution had failed to establish the conspiracy charges against the two CPM leaders. Those acquitted were Ganesan P (A2), Vijesh (A4), K Prakashan (A5), Umeshan V (A6), Latheesh C (A8), C N Mohanan (A11), Nithin (A13), Sudhakaran alias Conductor Sudhakaran (A17), Naveen N P (A18), Shyamjith (A19), Shaji (A21), Prakashan Muthuvani (A22), Ajayakumar N P (A23), Rajeevan P S (A24), K Babu (A29), U V Venu (A30), P Jayarajan (A32) and T V Rajesh (A33). A1 Sumesh was accused of plunging a dagger into Shukoor's chest, while A2 Ganesan was accused of stabbing Shukoor in the abdomen. Despite the testimony of eyewitness Zakaria, who was also stabbed, Ganesan was acquitted, and Sumesh convicted. What happened in February 2012 Shukoor, a 25-year-old MSF leader and treasurer of the MSF Taliparamba mandalam committee, was murdered at a paddy field at Valluvam Kadavu in Keezhara in Kannapuram panchayat on February 20, 2012. They were trying to run from a mob of CPM workers, who chased them to the house of one Mohammed Kunhi. They dragged Shukoor out of the house and stabbed him to death. Back then, it was widely reported that Shukoor was killed after he was tried in a kangaroo court of the CPM, surrounded by party workers. The violence had its immediate backdrop in an attack on CPM branch secretary Kunnool Rajan of Muthalappara, who was assaulted by a group of masked men while returning after distributing newspapers on February 19, 2012. Rajan suffered serious injuries, with both his legs broken after being beaten with iron rods. On February 20, Jayarajan, who was then the CPM Kannur district secretary, and Rajesh, the then Kalliasseri MLA, accompanied by journalists, visited the violence-hit area to see a reading room damaged in the clashes. Their vehicle was attacked by a group of people at Ariyil around 11 am. Several CPM workers and media personnel, including those from Kairali TV and Deshabhimani, were injured. Jayarajan and Rajesh later reached the Taliparamba police station with the injured and subsequently got them admitted to the Taliparamba Cooperative Hospital.
